items.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Little did we know, a couple of miles away, the same thing was happening with Ahmad Jamal. He was a student of Franz Liszt—I mean not a student, per se, but he was playing that sound.

ctx.x: Mary Elizabeth Fuller. She was the one that got lessons. There was a piano in our home, a big grand that she didn’t want my brother or I to touch. I would wait for Mr. Newton to come by to give her lessons. I would sit close by and I wrote. “Now, the piano is played like this. There’s 1-2-3-4-5 and 1-2-3 fingering. 1-2-3 and ­ 1-2-3-4-5.” That even got me. I’m over there listening and taking it all in. But she, at 11-years old was playing Franz Liszt. She came from the pool of kids, like…what was his name? Roland…
Playing that literature as a child.
